articles.title: Quote of the day by Fyodor Dostoevsky: "Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and…" - a powerful reminder to ask what you are really gaining from every sacrifice
articles.summary: Rest of World News: This line is one of the most quoted passages from Fyodor Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment, and it captures something genuinely powerful about self-be.
articles.body: This line is one of the most quoted passages from Fyodor Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment, and it captures something genuinely powerful about self-betrayal, regret and the choices people make when they lose sight of what actually matters to them. Unlike many quotes about failure that focus on losing money or opportunity, this line points at something considerably more personal, the real damage a person can do to themselves by repeatedly acting against their own values. It is especially relevant in a world where people often feel real pressure to fit in, please others, or simply appear successful. Someone may stay in a situation that genuinely makes them unhappy purely because they fear disappointing another person. Another may quietly give up an ambition simply because it never seemed practical enough to pursue properly, and yet years later they may find that the compromise achieved nothing at all worth having.Quote of the day by Fyodor Dostoevsky"Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing"Where this line actually comes fromThe quote comes from Part 4, Chapter 4 of Crime and Punishment, first published in 1866, and it is worth being genuinely accurate about its actual context. The line is not Dostoevsky speaking directly in his own voice. It is dialogue spoken by the character Svidrigaïlov, a genuinely unsettling and morally complicated figure in the novel, to Sonia, a young woman who has been forced into desperate circumstances to support her family. The fuller passage reads, "But you are a great sinner, that's true, and your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing. Isn't that fearful? Isn't it fearful that you are living in this filth which you loathe so, and at the same time you know yourself that you are not helping any one by it, not saving any one from anything." Dostoevsky, as the author, crafted this scene specifically to explore themes of guilt, sacrifice and self-destruction that run throughout the entire novel, and the line has genuinely outlived its original scene, circulating today as a standalone reflection on self-betrayal more broadly.What is the meaning of Fyodor Dostoevsky’s quoteThe real meaning here lies in the words "destroyed" and "betrayed." This is not describing an ordinary mistake. It describes what happens when someone repeatedly goes against their own conscience or their own values. To genuinely betray yourself can mean knowing exactly what you actually believe while choosing to act differently anyway, out of fear, pressure or simple convenience. It can happen gradually, rather than through one single dramatic decision. Someone may genuinely know that a particular friendship is unhealthy but keep maintaining it because they do not want to be alone. These decisions can feel necessary in the moment, but if they continue for too long, a person can genuinely begin to feel disconnected from who they actually are. The second half of the line, "for nothing," sharpens the whole message. Sacrificing yourself for a genuine purpose is a very different thing from destroying yourself for something that ultimately carries no real value at all.Why this quote still genuinely matters todayModern life creates countless real opportunities for people to compare themselves against each other. Social media and constant professional competition can make it genuinely tempting to change yourself simply to gain approval. People can spend years chasing a career purely because it looks impressive from the outside, even while it genuinely leaves them unhappy. This line encourages a genuinely different kind of self-examination instead. Before making a major compromise, it is worth honestly asking what exactly is being sacrificed, and what is actually being gained in return.The real difference between sacrifice and genuine self-betrayalNot every difficult choice actually means a person is betraying themselves. People regularly make genuine sacrifices for their children, their families or a long-term goal, and the important question is always whether the sacrifice genuinely serves something meaningful. Self-betrayal happens when a person keeps abandoning what actually matters to them without any clear purpose behind it, constantly saying yes when they genuinely want to say no, or giving up an important ambition purely out of fear of other people's opinions. A useful distinction is this: genuine sacrifice should take you somewhere. Self-betrayal can leave you feeling like you have lost yourself without gaining anything real in return.Know what genuinely matters to youPeople can make genuinely poor decisions when they do not have a clear sense of their own values. Knowing what actually matters most makes it considerably easier to recognise when a situation is asking you to compromise too much.Do not confuse approval with genuine happinessBeing accepted by absolutely everyone is genuinely impossible. Constantly changing yourself to satisfy other people can eventually leave you genuinely unsure about what you actually want for yourself.Think honestly about the cost of your choicesEvery major decision genuinely involves a trade-off. Before making a real sacrifice, it helps to consider both sides honestly, asking what you are actually giving up and whether the result is genuinely worth it.Learn to recognise when enough is genuinely enoughPersistence is genuinely valuable, but persistence in the wrong situation can become quietly damaging. Walking away from something that repeatedly harms your sense of self is not always failure. Sometimes it is genuinely self-respect instead.Other famous quotes by Fyodor Dostoevsky"Man only likes to count his troubles; he doesn't calculate his happiness.""Above all, don't lie to yourself. The man who lies to himself and listens to his own lie comes to a point that he cannot distinguish the truth within him, or around him, and so loses all respect for himself.""To go wrong in one's own way is better than to go right in someone else's.""Taking a new step, uttering a new word, is what people fear most."How to apply this quote in daily lifeThis message does not require any dramatic change. It can genuinely begin with small acts of honesty instead. Before agreeing to something, it helps to ask whether you genuinely want to do it, or whether you are simply afraid of disappointing someone else. When considering a career decision, it helps to think beyond salary or prestige and ask whether the work actually fits the life you genuinely want. The same principle applies to relationships too. If you repeatedly have to hide your feelings or pretend to be someone else simply to keep a relationship functioning, it may be worth genuinely examining what that relationship is actually costing you.Why this timeless message still resonatesThis line from Crime and Punishment is ultimately about the genuine value of remaining true to yourself. Life will always involve genuinely difficult decisions and real compromise, and the goal was never to avoid every situation that causes discomfort. The deeper lesson is understanding why you are actually making a sacrifice, and whether it genuinely serves something meaningful. "Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing" works as both a warning and a genuine reminder. Before sacrificing an important part of yourself, it helps to pause and ask what you are actually gaining in return.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Built in 1896, the historic five-story St Louis National Cash Register building spans 12,000 sq ft and is up for sale; once listed for $1.4M, it now asks $800,000
articles.summary: News News: ‘The Cosmopolitan’ in St Louis, Missouri, is no ordinary home. Built in 1896, this historic St Louis building once housed the National Cash Register c.
articles.body: ‘The Cosmopolitan’ in St Louis, Missouri, is no ordinary home. Built in 1896, this historic St Louis building once housed the National Cash Register company. Originally built as a place for commerce, the kind of sturdy brick-and-mortar operation that once anchored downtown, the property is now up for sale, according to Realtor.com.The five-story structure is now listed for $800,000, nearly half of its initial asking price of $1.4 million, in less than four years. That's $75 per square foot for a 12,000-square-foot Gothic Revival building in downtown. The buyer is not merely investing in an ordinary house, but an enormous historic building that looks and feels like an art museum, and they get to live and work in it.Historic five-story buildingThe St Louis historic building has had many owners before finally being listed again. After National Cash Register’s tenure, the building became a showroom for Clark Peeper furniture. Then came the interior designers Mark and Mary Pitliangas, who saw something in the bones that others might have overlooked. Not a fixer-upper, but a canvas. Known for their artistic endeavours, they had also restored a retro landmark in the form of a 25.5-foot-tall Vess Soda Bottle.What they built inside this building is almost impossible to describe without walking through it. The first floor is a Gothic lounge that feels pulled from another century. The travertine floors, custom stone and tilework, and illuminated stained glass run throughout the building. There are ceiling murals. There's a fireplace that was rescued from somewhere else and given new purpose here. The couple selected high-end antiques for features ranging from lighting to wall treatments, including a bar they retrofitted from an antique Chicago piece. And the best part? A brass elevator connects the five-story building.Five floors with numerous possibilitiesThe buyer is not getting an ordinary building. In fact, this historic building can transform into almost anything. Each level is curated differently. Every floor is fully zoned for both commercial and residential activities, which means buyers aren't locked into a single vision. The mezzanine functions as office and meeting space. The third floor holds a residential loft. The fourth could be a studio, storage, or a gallery. The penthouse is, of course, unlike anything. It features travertine floors, illuminated stained glass, ceiling buttresses, and modern amenities including Viking appliances and a home theatre.This historic building is not a cash register factory or a furniture store anymore. It is ready to become anything you want. The 12,000 sq ft building can be a private residence, an office building, or both.Treasure trove for antiquesThe building is a treasure trove for antiques, including custom tile, glasswork, and hand-painted artwork. Even the ceilings are embellished. Much of the furniture and antiques were either made or purchased specifically for The Cosmopolitan and will stay with the property. Some pieces are sentimental to the Pitliangases. Others are inventory from their design business, Antique Architectural Decor, which sources and installs custom materials for clients across the country. This is a bonus for buyers. You're not just purchasing walls and floors, but inheriting a curated collection of unique art pieces.The building has been on the market since 2022. Over the years, the price has fluctuated depending on market trends. Initially, The Cosmopolitan was listed for $1.4 million, but they didn’t really find any buyers. So they lowered the price. Now the asking price is $800,000, which means the price per square foot is roughly $100 less than the current Missouri average.“The ideal buyer is someone with flair and a desire to create unique experiences—whether that’s short-term rentals, creative offices, artist spaces, or the most singular home in the city,” previous listing agent Justin Ströhm told the outlet when the property first hit the market.No one is pretending that The Cosmopolitan is a starter property or an investment flip. But it's a statement. It’s an extraordinary building, so, of course, the buyers should match the vibe. They should understand that maintaining Gothic Revival architecture, custom tilework, and a brass elevator requires the kind of obsessive attention the Pitliangases had for the past two decades. The right person will see the 130-year-old building for what it is.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Worcestershire field investigated over medical waste dumping claims
articles.summary: The Environment Agency is leading an investigation into the site off Mill Lane, near Wadborough.
articles.body:
Land that borders a protected nature site is being investigated over claims it is being used as an illegal site to dump medical waste.

The Environment Agency (EA) said it was investigating the site off Mill Lane, near Wadborough, in Worcestershire. The land is near Great Blaythorn Meadow, which is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI).

A resident in the area, who asked not to be named, told the BBC a muck spreader, which are normally used to distribute farmyard manure, had been used to spread medical waste.

The EA said it was investigating alongside West Mercia Police, Wychavon District Council and Worcestershire County Council.

An EA spokesperson said: "Waste crime scars communities and the environment and, in line with our 10-point plan, we're acting quickly to tackle illegal activity."

The resident said they were concerned by how close the site was in relation to Great Blaythorn Meadow, which Natural England lists as an SSSI.

Natural England considers the land special for its biological interest, specifically wanting to protect its rare lowland meadow and grassland habitat.

The resident claimed "local residents of Wadborough and Drakes Broughton had identified some of the spread waste as medical in origin" and "estimated that 300 tonnes of contaminated waste has been spread on the field".

However, the EA has not confirmed the nature of the waste or how much waste has been dumped.

Photos said to be taken at the scene show small scraps of metal and plastic scattered across the area which is under investigation.

In December 2025, the BBC revealed a site off Mill Lane was under investigation for illegal waste dumping .

At the time, it became the third site in Worcestershire being investigated for illegal waste dumping.

The others sites were Stone Arrow Farm, Peopleton and Haselor Lane, Evesham.

The EA said it was "pulling every lever available" to "disrupt those who profit from the harm illegal waste sites cause".

articles.title: Hong Kong or Singapore: Which country should expats choose in 2026?
articles.summary: News News: Hong Kong and Singapore are Asia's two most important international countries that offer strong opportunities for expats in terms of career, public tr.
articles.body: Hong Kong and Singapore are Asia's two most important international countries that offer strong opportunities for expats in terms of career, public transportation, and they also provide access to some of the world's most dynamic business markets.However, the rivalry between these two countries is famous and heating up again. These two countries are top financial hubs that are mulling tax breaks for fund managers, as per the latest move made to keep the high-earning finance jobs, and it happened after decade. Hong Kong's population has undergone a transformation in recent years.They have reshaped their local businesses, nightlife, and private schools. Most of the expats have returned to their city after an exodus during the Covid-19 pandemic and also the aftermath of violent pro-democracy protests.The visas for foreign white-collar professionals have levelled up in Singapore after a surge as the city-state got more selective about that. But high-end homes, wealth management, and luxury sales are still supported by the wealthy foreigners, according to the Bloomberg report. Living in Singapore and living in Hong Kong is very different. If we talk about Singapore, then it is generally more spacious, structured, full of greenery and predictable. On the other hand, living in Hong Kong is denser as it's a fast-paced city with an energetic vibe, and it is closely connected with China.Let's check out which city is better to live in:Quality of lifeSingapore is usually a well-organized and more relaxing city. This is known for its cleanliness, safety, better public transportation, and it has a lot of greenery. People can use the English language, which is anyway a better option, as it makes everyday life easy for international residents.Hong Kong is an extremely populated and fast-paced city. It gives a feel of an urban environment because it is fully crowded. There are various restaurants, entertainment places, shopping malls and cultural attractions.It has beaches and hiking trails, so people are more attracted to this place. People are more drawn to this because it is appealing to outdoor enthusiasts.There are so many aspects on which people can think when selecting the perfect city for their survival, and here we are going to give the key points so you can check them below:How much can I earn?There are top finance jobs available in Hong Kong that pay more than those in Singapore, but not as much as before, as the gap has narrowed since four years ago.The dollar rate in Singapore has strengthened and the firms in Hong Kong can no longer give the huge incentives during the years of Covid. The wage gap was more than 60% in the year 2022 for director and chief-level positions. The investment banker pay shows a greater gap between these two cities.The top rainmakers earn 15% more than the people earn in Singapore, said John Mullally, managing director of Hong Kong at Robert Walters, as quoted by Bloomberg.Housing facilityThere is a mixture of public and private housing in Singapore. There are various residents living in HDB apartments, and on the other hand, expatriates and higher-income people prefer living in landed properties.As compared to Hong Kong, Singapore offers more space for the money. However, living in the desirable central areas could be more expensive. articles.title: Divers uncover hundreds of ancient relics near shipwreck untouched for 2,100 years
articles.summary: Pictures show hundreds of intact amphorae scattered across the seabed near Mazara del Vallo, where a Roman shipwreck lay hidden for over 2,000 years.
articles.body: Archaeologists recently uncovered a roughly 2,100-year-old shipwreck off the coast of Sicily — along with hundreds of remnants of its ancient cargo. The discovery was announced last month by the Italian Ministry of Culture. The ruins are about three miles off the coast of Mazara del Vallo, a city located about 50 miles southwest of Palermo. The wreck was discovered during a joint inspection by Italian cultural heritage officials and Carabinieri diving units after private citizens reported the site. MYSTERY OF GOLD COIN SHIPWRECK FINALLY UNMASKED AFTER 30 YEARS: 'FANTASTIC CONCLUSION' The Roman-era wreck dates between the second and first centuries B.C., the ministry said. Divers found the site at a depth of about 150 feet. "Hundreds of amphorae, predominantly of the Dressel 1A type, are present on the seabed, along with two lead anchor stocks and another structure made of the same material," officials said in a translated statement. Pictures show hundreds of ancient amphorae clustered across the seabed, many still remarkably intact despite spending more than 2,000 years underwater. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Amphorae, ceramic vessels commonly used throughout the ancient world, were often used to carry wine and olive oil, though officials have not said what the vessels found aboard the wreck once contained. In a statement, Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli called the find "one of the most important underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years." He added, "The sea continues to return precious fragments of our history to us, and the Mazara del Vallo shipwreck tells us about the people, routes and trade that made the Mediterranean a crossroads of civilizations." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "Research will continue to uncover its history and make it available to the public." Sicily's Superintendency of the Sea will conduct further research to learn more about the site's history and establish measures to protect it. articles.title: Surrey's incoming councils eyeing tourism tax to boost funds
articles.summary: A small overnight stay levy would apply to the likes of hotels, bed and breakfasts and guesthouses.
articles.body:
Surrey's two new unitary authorities are considering a tourism tax to help buoy their finances.

This "overnight visitor levy", which regional mayors will be allowed to charge under government plans, could come to the county as part of a major overhaul of its councils.

East and West Surrey councils are set to take over power from Surrey County Council and the 11 district councils next April, after which they plan to pool resources on certain services.

A government spokesperson said the levy would "ensure local people and economies keep more of the rewards and invest in what matters most to their communities, including reinvesting back into tourism itself".

The move would allow regional mayors to impose a small tax on paid visitor accommodation in their areas, the aim of which is to see more investment in local infrastructure.

This would apply to hotels, bed and breakfasts and guesthouses, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service .

A cabinet statement in July said the government would give "all strategic authorities the ability to introduce an overnight visitor levy, with local leaders able to set out plans for how revenues will be invested by March 2028".

A government spokesperson added that similar levies in other countries typically add only a small amount per night and have limited impact on visitor numbers and jobs.

MeanwhiIe, a 2019 study by the Institute for Fiscal Studies estimated that a £1 tourist tax could raise £420 million per year across England.

articles.title: Macklemore defends 'Free Palestine' call after Ed Sheeran tour backlash
articles.summary: Some ticket buyers called for the rapper to be removed from the tour after he made the comments.
articles.body:
Rapper Macklemore has said his recent calls to "Free Palestine" while on tour with singer Ed Sheeran in the US were not intended as an attack on Jewish people.

There had been calls for the 43-year-old to be removed from Sheeran's tour after he made the comments while supporting the singer at two live dates in New Jersey over the weekend.

In a video posted on his social media channels on Monday, Macklemore was seen on stage saying: "To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters: Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide, is in no way a criticism of you."

Israel rejects allegations of genocide. It says its troops conduct self-defence operations in Gaza and the occupied West Bank in accordance with international law.

The Israeli military launched a campaign in Gaza in response to the unprecedented Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 were taken hostage.

More than 73,000 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since then - more than 1,300 since a ceasefire declared on 10 October 2025, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are seen as reliable by the UN.

The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is currently hearing a case brought by South Africa that accuses Israeli forces of genocide, but it could take years to reach a conclusion. Israel has called the case "wholly unfounded" and based on "biased and false claims".

Macklemore made his initial comments at Sheeran's New Jersey shows on Friday and Saturday as he introduced his 2024 protest song Hind's Hall, which condemns Israel's military action in Gaza.

After the rapper made his comments, the Israeli-American Council launched a petition urging Sheeran to remove Macklemore as his support act for the remainder of the tour.

The petition said Macklemore had "used the stage to deliver an extended political message, called for 'Free Palestine' and performed Hind's Hall while images from Gaza and other political messaging were projected across the stadium screens".

The council said the event was a concert, "not a political rally, not a protest, and not an activist event".

It added: "This becomes even more troubling when the message relies on selective imagery, biased messaging, and disputed claims presented to a massive audience as fact, without context or complexity."

Some ticket buyers posted messages addressed to Sheeran on social media criticising Macklemore's involvement in the tour, but the rapper also received praise and support from some fans, and his comments have received tens of thousands of shares.

On Monday, Macklemore uploaded a video on his social media feeds captioned: "Wanting all humans to be treated equal[ly] should never be controversial."

In the footage, he is seen saying: "One of the reasons I wanted to come on this tour was because I wanted to stand up on stages across America and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine.

"I want those words to be loud and clear so the people from Gaza all the way to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten them."

He concluded: "My message is for peace, love, for all human beings to be treated equally and with dignity."

BBC News has asked representatives for Ed Sheeran for a response to the calls for Macklemore to be removed as his support act.

Sheeran has been on his Loop tour in support of his latest album Play since January, but Macklemore only joined him as a support act recently as part of the US leg.

The rapper is also scheduled to join Sheeran at further US dates in the coming weeks.

In 2014, Macklemore apologised for a costume he wore on stage, which critics said was antisemitic.

articles.title: Scenes of 'mayhem' after fatal crash near Edinburgh Airport
articles.summary: Police have launched a search for two women and a man following the crash on the A8 on Monday.
articles.body:
Residents living close to the scene of a fatal multi-car crash near Edinburgh Airport have described scenes of "mayhem" in the aftermath of the incident.

Vehicles were said to be "strewn across two lanes" following the crash involving a grey Mercedes A250, a black Renault Captur, a grey Skoda Karoq and a grey Hyundai i30 on the A8 Glasgow Road at about 09:25 on Monday.

A 58-year-old woman, who was driving the Hyundai, died at the scene.

Police Scotland have since launched a search for two women and a man thought to have fled the Mercedes into a nearby field on foot afterwards.

Officers deployed a helicopter and a dog unit as part of the operation.

Four other people were taken to hospital for treatment after the crash but were later released.

The road was closed for almost 10 hours before reopening at about 19:05.

Tom Brumfitt, who lives in one of the small row of cottages by the side of the road, said he heard "loud bangs" as he lay in bed when the collision happened.

Brumfitt, 69, said a man screaming "help" and "shouting for his mum" ran past the window a short time later, but it was unclear how he was involved in the crash.

He said: "It was just mayhem. It was the worst scenario I had seen outside for a long time.

"There was an almighty bang, a van partly on its side and then someone running past shouting 'help, help, help'.

"By the time I had got out, they had gone. The helicopter was over us later on, obviously looking for the people involved."

Christine Yule, 75, said her son, who has special needs, had just left their house in a taxi.

She said she was "frantic" with worry before seeing him walking with the taxi driver on the opposite side of the road.

She said he was "really upset" by the crash but was otherwise unharmed.

Police Scotland have launched an appeal for information .

The Scottish Ambulance Service said it had dispatched three ambulances, two special operations response teams, a paramedic response unit and a critical care paramedic.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service also attended the incident.

Paul Dow said he was in his house working when he heard "several large crashes and bangs" as the collision took place.

He said he opened his front door to see smashed vehicles scattered across the eastbound and westbound carriageways after being told about the incident by a neighbour.

Dow, 49, said it was "not unusual" for there to be crashes on that stretch of road, however, it was clear this one was far more severe.

"Most of the crashes here are fairly simple nose to tails, nothing too serious," he said.

"But it was quite apparent there was going to be a fatality in this one and it's horrific that people would consider driving the way they did on this road.

Insp Thomas Mallinson said: "My thoughts are with the family of the person who died at this incredibly difficult time.

"Our inquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances of this crash, and it is vital we trace the three people who left the area before police arrived."

articles.title: Retaliatory Canadian tariffs take effect
articles.summary: Canada’s retaliatory tariffs on $27.6 billion in American products took effect on Tuesday, marking the latest escalation in an ongoing trade fight between the U.S. and its northern neighbor. The economic policies impose 15 percent, 25 percent and 50 percent tariffs on around 6 percent of what the U.S. exported to Canada last year. The…
articles.body:
Canada’s retaliatory tariffs on $27.6 billion in American products took effect on Tuesday, marking the latest escalation in an ongoing trade fight between the U.S. and its northern neighbor.

The economic policies impose 15 percent, 25 percent and 50 percent tariffs on around 6 percent of what the U.S. exported to Canada last year. The tariffs cover a range of more than 700 U.S. products, including metals, clothing, appliances, cosmetics and farming products.

Last month, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney threatened to match new U.S. tariffs “dollar for dollar” after he pulled Canada’s negotiators from trade talks with the U.S. just hours before the Trump administration’s 50 percent tariffs went into effect.

The U.S. tariffs apply to more than $20 billion in Canadian goods, ranging from hockey sticks to wine to cement. Carney has criticized the action as a “ direct violation ” of the free trade agreement between the U.S., Canada and Mexico.

On Tuesday, Canada doubled its tariffs on U.S. steel and aluminum to 50 percent — a direct match on the 50 percent tariffs the U.S. imposed on these products from Canada.

Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said when announcing the counter tariffs last month that they were “designed primarily to provide protection for Canadian industries impacted by the U.S. tariffs and allow them to compete against U.S. products in the Canadian market.”

President Trump hit back immediately, threatening Canada with new 50 percent tariffs on imported cars, trucks, auto parts and steel to take effect on New Year’s Day.

“Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years,” Trump wrote on Truth Social following Canada’s announcement of its retaliatory tariffs last month.

“Their ridiculously high tariffs on our Farmers and farm products has made life impossible for these great American Patriots, and has long created a 60 Billion Dollar Deficit between our two Countries,” he continued. “Not sustainable, and NOT ANYMORE!”

The president said Canada will no longer “be treated like a State.”

Trump has repeatedly suggested the U.S. trading partner could be ceded as a U.S. state, sharing a map of the two countries covered in the American flag in a Monday Truth Social post .

On Monday, the president also threatened to block the sale of Canada’s Bombardier aircraft unless they move manufacturing to the U.S.

“If they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a ‘piggybank,’” he wrote on Truth Social . “BUY AMERICAN. FLY ON AMERICAN AIRLINERS. ENJOY AMERICAN LIQUOR AND BEVERAGES. SAIL ON LAKE AMERICA. AMERICA FIRST!”

articles.title: Iceland summons US ambassador after Trump post showing American flag covering island
articles.summary: Iceland’s government called in the U.S. ambassador on Monday after President Trump posted a map showing the Nordic nation blanketed by the American flag. Trump, who has previously pushed to take over Greenland and Canada, posted an image to Truth Social of the American flag stretching across North America, Greenland, Iceland, Central America and the…
articles.body:
Iceland’s government called in the U.S. ambassador on Monday after President Trump posted a map showing the Nordic nation blanketed by the American flag.

Trump, who has previously pushed to take over Greenland and Canada, posted an image to Truth Social of the American flag stretching across North America, Greenland, Iceland, Central America and the Caribbean, with the map labeled “United States of America.”

Trump did not offer an explanation for the post.

Icelandic Foreign Minister Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir summoned U.S. Ambassador to Iceland Billy Long over the image, according to Icelandic public broadcaster RUV .

The Foreign Ministry told the outlet that officials made clear to Long, a former Missouri lawmaker and IRS commissioner who became ambassador in May, that Trump’s post was “completely inappropriate.”

Long himself had previously apologized for joking about Iceland becoming the 52nd U.S. state with himself as governor, which had caused widespread outrage from Icelandic citizens and prompted a petition to prevent his ambassadorship.

At a press conference Tuesday, Gunnarsdóttir said the message was “absurd” and insulting to Icelanders, as well as citizens of Greenland and Canada.

“There is nothing funny or normal about making fun of the sovereignty of states,” she said. “If this is supposed to be a joke, then it is a bad joke.”

While Trump has not formally pushed to take over Iceland in the past, Trump’s interest in acquiring Greenland, a semiautonomous territory, from Denmark has led to escalating tensions. Its leaders have said repeatedly that the island is not for sale and does not want to become part of the U.S.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen reiterated that position Monday while visiting Greenland’s capital city of Nuuk, saying its government and its residents have repeatedly made clear that they have no interest in being acquired.

“The Greenlandic government and the Greenlandic people have said again and again that they do not want to be American,” she told Danish news agency Ritzau. “I hope no one is in any doubt about that, either in the United States or the rest of the world.”

articles.title: Regime change is the only real solution to the Iran problem
articles.summary: In recent weeks, numerous reports have blamed U.S. involvement in the Ukraine and Iran wars for depleting U.S. weapons supplies. Most importantly, critics allege, America’s own self-defense capacity is jeopardized by the diversion of arms on behalf of others.
articles.body:
The Trump administration, like most of its predecessors, is busy scurrying around the world putting out individual fires set in dispersed locations — the Middle East, Ukraine, East Asia. All the while, its increasingly coordinated adversaries are intent on bringing about the demise of the Western international order that has brought overall global peace for three-quarters of a century.

In recent weeks, numerous reports have blamed U.S. involvement in the Ukraine and Iran wars for depleting U.S. weapons supplies needed to deter or defeat other potential challenges by Russia, China and North Korea. Most importantly, critics allege, America’s own self-defense capacity is jeopardized by the diversion of arms on behalf of others, either to help Ukraine repel Russia’s invasion or to protect the Middle East and the world from Iran’s nuclear threat.

Now, an official report from U.S. military officials to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth confirms that the “divide, distract and conquer” strategy of America’s enemies is succeeding. Washington is increasingly wary of undertaking additional U.S. security commitments — a reluctance bordering on isolationism that frees our adversaries to act out their aggression in other venues and exploit assorted targets of opportunity.

In addition, extended deployments of U.S. forces are taking a toll on the resilience and morale of Navy personnel. This week, the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier group arrived in Thailand from its 10-month tour to the region. The long deployment has substantially disrupted the ship’s maintenance.

The drain on munitions, equipment, personnel and the strategic attention of the U.S government all vindicate the collaboration among the members of the new evil empire. As the Trump administration takes actions against Iran in the military and economic realms, China, Russia, and North Korea are rushing to fill the gaps and bolster Iran’s position against the U.S., Israel and the West.

If these conditions are allowed to continue, there is little hope that Tehran will agree to abandon its nuclear ambitions, its oppression of its own people, or its support of terrorist and criminal activities in the region and beyond.

The present course of events is unsustainable.

America’s strategic credibility vis-a-vis not only Iran but all other governments that deal with the U.S., is being significantly diminished . The predictable outcome if the present course continues will constitute a major, and lasting, failure of U.S. policy in the region. That means that Iran, both on its own and through its participation with the other members of the authoritarian cabal, will persist in undermining the U.S. place in the world and the international order itself.

The only long-term solution to the 47-year-old Iran problem is the path on which President Trump originally started when he urged the Iranian population to rise up against the institutions of the regime. But because that exhortation was ill-timed and not coordinated with kinetic and information operations, the citizen protest that followed ended catastrophically , with tens of thousands of unarmed protestors killed and no intervention from Washington or allies. Iran’s odious regime is still there and now more vengeful than ever.

Along with his resumption of the bombing of Iran this week, Trump repeated his appeal to Iranians to “rise up” against the regime. But they would be justified in demanding to know how the U.S. would react differently this time to another brutal regime crackdown on the population.

Would the U.S., perhaps working with Israel or others, make a concerted effort to eliminate the remaining leadership of the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps? Would Trump finally cut off financial and material support from China and others? Will the U.S. and allies provide the defenseless Iranian population with the weapons needed to fight back against their murderous oppressors? Will they deploy boots on the ground to train and otherwise support an Iranian resistance, perhaps by establishing a protected liberation zone as a base from which to attack and isolate the regime?

These operations, together with a strategic communications campaign that restores the information agencies that the Trump administration foolishly dismantled , could finally bring the regime’s demise. The institutions that won the Cold War and helped overthrow the seemingly all-powerful Soviet Union — Voice of America, Radio Free Europe, the U.S. Information Agency and others — would be perfect instruments to amplify and coordinate Trump’s repeated but erratic calls for regime change in Iran.

Success here could earn Trump his coveted Nobel Prize and eclipse the shallow vanity projects he seeks to embellish his legacy.

Joseph Bosco served as China country director for the secretary of Defense from 2005 to 2006 and as Asia-Pacific director of humanitarian assistance and disaster relief from 2009 to 2010. He is a nonresident fellow at the Institute for Corean-American Studies, a member of the advisory board of the Global Taiwan Institute and member of the advisory board of the Vandenberg Coalition.

articles.title: Nelson Mandela grew up in this tiny South African village; his childhood landscape is now being preserved as a heritage centre
articles.summary: Rest of World News: On the rolling hills of South Africa’s Eastern Cape, Qunu remains a small rural village, much as it was when Nelson Mandela spent his childhood there..
articles.body: On the rolling hills of South Africa’s Eastern Cape, Qunu remains a small rural village, much as it was when Nelson Mandela spent his childhood there. There are no grand city streets or imposing landmarks to announce its place in history. Instead, the landscape holds quieter reminders of the boy who would later become South Africa’s first democratically elected president. A stone known as the Sliding Stone recalls the games of his childhood, while the Africa Native Mission Church marks where he was christened, as reported by Nelson Mandela Museum.Nearby are other places tied to his early years, including the remains of a school and sites connected with his family. Today, the Nelson Mandela Youth and Heritage Centre brings these fragments together within a wider effort to preserve Qunu’s heritage. The centre also serves a practical purpose, with programmes focused on education, leadership, arts and opportunities for young people in the surrounding community.How Qunu preserves the childhood story of Nelson MandelaThe village is part of a wider trail of places connected with Mandela’s life in the Eastern Cape. Qunu was where he grew up and started school, while nearby Mqhekezweni was where he spent much of his youth. Mvezo, his birthplace, is also part of the broader heritage landscape associated with his life.What makes Qunu different is the concentration of childhood landmarks that have survived there. The Nelson Mandela Youth and Heritage Centre sits in the village and was created as a place through which visitors could encounter the less public part of his biography; his beginnings, rather than the better-known years of political leadership and imprisonment.The centre’s role is not limited to displaying objects. It also supports learning, leadership programmes and activities involving young people.How a simple stone and church is connected with Mandela’s childhoodAmong the features at Qunu is a large stone associated with Mandela’s childhood. Known as the Sliding Stone, it is remembered as a place where Mandela played with other boys from the village.It is a modest piece of the landscape, and that is part of its significance. Unlike a formal monument, the stone points towards the ordinary routines of childhood; the sort of place that might otherwise have disappeared from the historical record.The stone remains among the places included in guided visits around Qunu, allowing visitors to follow locations associated with Mandela’s early life.Another surviving place is the Africa Native Mission Church in Qunu. It is identified as the church where Mandela, then known by his birth name Rolihlahla, was christened.The church adds another layer to the village’s story. Mandela’s childhood was shaped by both the traditions of his Thembu upbringing and the institutions introduced through missionary education. His early schooling and Christian upbringing became part of the environment in which his character and outlook developed.The church is therefore presented as part of the physical history of Qunu rather than as a separate attraction. Visitors moving through the area encounter a landscape made up of homes, religious buildings, school sites and other places associated with Mandela’s early years.Qunu’s heritage centre gives Mandela’s legacy a living roleThe Youth and Heritage Centre was built with a purpose that extends beyond tourism. It was established to support youth and community development through education, leadership programmes and activities involving arts, crafts and heritage.That approach reflects an idea associated with Mandela’s vision for the museum. He did not want it to become simply a static tribute to him. The intention was for his legacy to contribute to the development of the surrounding community.The Qunu centre has consequently been used for educational activities and youth programmes. Its facilities include accommodation, conference and catering spaces, exhibition areas and sporting facilities, allowing it to function as more than a conventional museum site.According to the Nelson Mandela Museum’s Annual Performance Plan of 2024–25, tour guide services around the Qunu site had resumed and local schools were using its facilities for educational programmes. The museum also described the centre as a place intended to create opportunities for young people and women in the surrounding community.Qunu’s museum site returns to public life after closureAs reported by the Department of Public Works, the centre’s development has not been uninterrupted. It was closed in 2019 while maintenance and renovation work was carried out.According to the South African Government website, Qunu reopened to the public on 18 July 2023, when Mandela statues were unveiled at the museum’s sites in Qunu and Mthatha. The reopening restored a venue that had previously been used for educational programmes and community activities.The wider site also includes family graves, a rondavel associated with his early years, his former home and his burial place. Together, these locations create a record of the different stages of his connection with Qunu.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Newsom: Condemnation of Netanyahu ‘almost universal’ among Democrats
articles.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) said Monday that condemnation of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is “almost universal” in the Democratic Party. In an interview with PBS News’s “Settle In,” host Amna Nawaz asked Newsom about the Democratic stance on Israel, which has divided the party in battleground states such as Michigan. “I think it’s…
articles.body:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) said Monday that condemnation of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is “almost universal” in the Democratic Party.

In an interview with PBS News’s “ Settle In ,” host Amna Nawaz asked Newsom about the Democratic stance on Israel, which has divided the party in battleground states such as Michigan.

“I think it’s overwhelmingly opposed to the current regime in Israel,” he said.

“You believe the party is?” Nawaz clarified.

“The condemnation of what Netanyahu is doing is almost universal,” Newsom responded. “There’s no controversy within the party on that.”

He cited Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and Netanyahu’s rejection of a two-state solution as reasons behind the condemnation.

“We want a democratic and secure Israel, and we want a secure democratic Palestinian state as well, right next door, and I don’t think that’s a really divisive thing,” he said.

“Even if you don’t think it’s a genocide, it’s a moral catastrophe how things have been conducted,” he added.

Newsom — a potential 2028 presidential contender — previously compared Israel to an “apartheid state” in March, even suggesting that the United States should “rethink” its relationship with Israel. Earlier in the year, he also told conservative commentator Ben Shapiro on the governor’s podcast “This is Gavin Newsom” in January that he was “crystal clear on my love for Israel.”

Nawaz asked Newsom about donations from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) — a major pro-Israel group — becoming a “litmus test for candidates.”

“But again, it’s pretty overwhelming opposition to accepting money from AIPAC as well,” he said. “I think it’s a minority of Democrats that are accepting AIPAC.”

Newsom confirmed in February that he has never accepted money from AIPAC and will not in the future.

Public opinion of Israel in the U.S. has shifted in the years since the Israeli government launched its military offensive in Gaza after Oct. 7, 2023.

An Associated Press/NORC poll found that 58 percent of Democrats believe the U.S. supports Israel too much. It reported that 62 percent of Democrats say the U.S. has not supported Palestinians enough, compared with 49 percent in 2024.

articles.title: 'Releasing 6,000 cusecs is impossible': Karnataka on Cauvery water order, may move Supreme Court
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Karnataka government is seriously considering approaching the Supreme Court against the direction to release 6,000 cusecs of Cauvery ri.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Karnataka government is seriously considering approaching the Supreme Court against the direction to release 6,000 cusecs of Cauvery river water daily to Tamil Nadu, state water resources minister N Chaluvarayaswamy said on Tuesday.The Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) on Tuesday recommended that Karnataka ensure a flow of 6,000 cusecs to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.The recommendation was subsequently upheld by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA).Chaluvarayaswamy described the CWRC order as "absurd" and said Karnataka was facing a difficult situation because inflows into the Cauvery basin had declined significantly over the past week."Our officials strongly argued the ground realities at the CWRC meeting. Tamil Nadu had sought 17,000 cusecs of water. However, inflows into the Cauvery basin have declined considerably over the past week. articles.title: Russia resumes strikes on Kyiv after pause for US envoys’ visit
articles.summary: Russia resumed strikes on Kyiv and across Ukraine early on Tuesday following a pause in attacks that allowed President Trump’s top envoys for peace negotiations to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in the country’s capital. The Ukrainian military downed 175 aerial targets, the Ministry of Defense said, but added that ballistic missiles hit homes in Kyiv,…
articles.body:
Russia resumed strikes on Kyiv and across Ukraine early on Tuesday following a pause in attacks that allowed President Trump’s top envoys for peace negotiations to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in the country’s capital.

The Ukrainian military downed 175 aerial targets, the Ministry of Defense said , but added that ballistic missiles hit homes in Kyiv, a market in Odesa and a train in the Sumy region.

“The russians bombed us all night. Kyiv was exploding and burning. We were all hiding in shelters,” the European Union’s ambassador to Ukraine, Katarina Mathernova, posted on the social platform X .

Two civilians were killed, the ministry said. At least 19 people were wounded in Kyiv, and fires broke out in 14 high-rise buildings, a dorm, a school, a clinic, warehouses and other sites, Reuters reported , citing Ukrainian officials.

The Russian attacks came shortly after Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff left Kyiv after meeting with Zelensky on Monday, tasked with restarting negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv to end the more than four-and-a-half-year war. Both Russia and Ukraine had agreed to a three-day ceasefire to allow for Kushner and Witkoff’s travel.

Kushner, the president’s son-in-law, and Witkoff, the president’s longtime friend and business partner, had earlier met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. They then traveled to Kyiv, marking the first time they visited the Ukrainian capital. Witkoff said he had visited Moscow at least eight times as part of Trump’s efforts to end the war.

The envoys said they put forward “new ideas” to end the war, although they did not provide details publicly. Kushner said they are in touch with Ukrainian officials almost daily.

Facing a press conference in Kyiv on Monday, Kushner and Witkoff defended their diplomatic efforts despite failing to achieve a ceasefire in a war that Trump promised to end within 24 hours of returning to office. A reporter noted that negotiations to end the war with Iran and bring peace to Gaza weren’t going much better.

“The tone of your question was a little bit like, why haven’t you done every single impossible thing possible? We are very honored to be able to have the opportunity to work on these under President Trump’s leadership,” Kushner responded.

“We have been doing everything we can to try and find a way out of a mess that was created before President Trump’s time.”

Zelensky, speaking at the press conference, said he discussed with Witkoff, Kushner and European partners present for the talks about scaling up defensive materials for the winter to combat an expected increase in Russian ballistic missile attacks against Ukrainian energy infrastructure and civilian sites. Ukraine is pleading with the U.S. and other allies to provide critical air defenses — particularly Patriot interceptors — to counter Russian ballistic missiles.

“We are counting on support for air defense and the energy sector, as well as substantial volumes of American LNG [liquified natural gas] and the ability to use them,” Zelensky said, in remarks translated in a post on X.

The Ukrainian leader said sticking points in talks with Russia remain, specifically around territory that Russia wants to claim in any peace deal, and said these must be discussed between the country’s leaders. Putin has mocked Zelensky as an illegitimate leader, conditioned any leader-level talks on the Ukrainian president traveling to Moscow, and called for elections to take place in Ukraine before any leader-level talks.

“I think such complex issues can only be resolved at the level of leaders,” Zelensky said.

“But the main thing is that today we have the opportunity to discuss everything — security guarantees, Ukraine’s future and the prosperity plan. We are talking not only about security guarantees, but also about economic guarantees for Ukraine — to recover and rebuild.”

articles.title: Trump-Carney AI hockey video stirs anger while racking up views
articles.summary: A video shared by a popular account supportive of President Trump on the social platform X that depicts him repeatedly beating Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney with a hockey stick has gained traction this week amid an escalating trade fight between the U.S. and Canada. The clip, which had garnered hundreds of thousands of views from…
articles.body:
A video shared by a popular account supportive of President Trump on the social platform X that depicts him repeatedly beating Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney with a hockey stick has gained traction this week amid an escalating trade fight between the U.S. and Canada.

The clip , which had garnered hundreds of thousands of views from reposts on X as of Tuesday, is an animation of an image shared by Trump on Truth Social on Sunday.

Its circulation online comes as Canada’s new retaliatory tariffs on a large swath of U.S. imports took effect on Tuesday morning.

The original artwork shared by the president over the weekend depicted him and the Canadian leader in hockey gear, with Carney lying on the ice and Trump leaning over him, saying, “Get up, Governor.”

The animated version of the image was first shared by an account titled Commentary Trump Daily Posts, which has no official ties to the president or the White House. The doctored clip depicts Trump yelling and striking Carney with his hockey stick until the Canadian leader collapses on the ice.

“President Trump just posted this image on Truth Social and we brought it to life!” the commentary account wrote in a post alongside the animation.

The fan account’s doctored video was quick to provoke anger online, much of it from familiar critics of the president. Many of those voices tied the clip to the president, even though the White House and Trump did not send out the video.

George Conway, a frequent critic of the president and the ex-husband of Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign manager, Kellyanne Conway, responded to a post that inaccurately made it appear as though the president shared the video himself.

“He’s deeply mentally ill,” Conway wrote in an X post on Monday evening that had more than 246,000 views as of Tuesday morning.

Political commentator and former sports broadcaster Keith Olbermann also slammed the video. It was not clear whether Olbermann was aware the video was produced by an account independent of the White House and Trump.

“If the animation in which Trump beats Carney with a hockey stick showed the reverse and were distributed by Carney… Trump and his criminal cult would be demanding Carney be arrested for threatening a head of state,” he wrote in an X post .

Olbermann added, “Canada should demand Trump’s arrest and extradition.”

Additionally, Sarah Longwell, the founder of Republican Voters Against Trump and the Republican Accountability Project, said it was “not that hard to see that Trump has been reduced to relying on AI to make him look tough and capable.”

“Because in reality he knows he looks like he’s weak and failing,” Longwell wrote on X in response to the photo animation. Her post had more than 32,000 views as of Tuesday morning.

Many of those recirculating the clip, including Longwell and Olbermann, were sharing a post by the author Amy Siskand that had more than 730,000 views as of Tuesday morning.

The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment.

The president has shared a series of Truth Social posts critical of Carney and Canada on Truth Social in recent weeks amid the escalating trade fight between the two trading partners. Trump has repeatedly threatened to make Canada the 51st U.S. state and referred to Carney as a “governor.”

On Monday, the president posted a map of the U.S. and Canada covered in an American flag and the words “United States of America.”

Carney and other Canadian officials have brushed off the president’s insults and urged the U.S. to refocus on trade deal negotiations.

“When the Americans stop doing memes, stop throwing shade and stop trying to be tough, and start being serious about having those discussions, we can have those discussions,” the Canadian leader said last week , according to The Associated Press.

“It’s not constructive, but that’s their democracy,” Carney added.

articles.title: Colorado TPUSA chapter enrollment 'flat' after elderly supporter was stricken by student with Taco Bell cup
articles.summary: Video captured the chaos after Fort Lewis College approved a Turning Point USA chapter, but nearly a year later, membership remains stagnant.
articles.body: Enrollment at the Turning Point USA (TPUSA) chapter at Fort Lewis College in Durango, Colorado, remains flat due to students’ fears of retaliation, according to chapter leaders and local supporters. The stagnation comes nearly a year after the campus group's registration sparked intense pushback from the surrounding community and student body. "It's definitely been flat, I would say," Rachel Cook, vice president of the Fort Lewis College chapter, told Fox News Digital. Cook’s comments come nearly a year after the student government's decision to recognize the chapter touched off severe turmoil on campus — much of which was captured on video and obtained by Fox News Digital. ERIKA KIRK URGES CONSERVATIVE STUDENTS NOT TO BACK DOWN IN FIRST SCHOOL YEAR SINCE CHARLIE'S ASSASSINATION One video showed a student being detained by campus police after striking 66-year-old local resident David Peters with a Taco Bell cup outside the student senate chambers. Peters, former chair of the La Plata County GOP and a retired Chevron executive, reflected on the incident and its lingering effect on the student group. "Their membership has been essentially flat. The issue is that a lot of students are reluctant to join the chapter for fear of retaliation," Peters said. "And their fears are well-founded. There have been some members who have received anonymous death threats." Cook echoed those safety concerns. "One of the main things is that students have said they are hesitant to join because of their personal safety. A lot of our officers have been getting threats and being harassed," she said. UC BERKELEY SUED FOR ALLEGEDLY STONEWALLING PROBE INTO VIOLENT AMBUSH AT TPUSA ROB SCHNEIDER EVENT The tensions at Fort Lewis College unfolded amid a national surge in interest for TPUSA campus chapters. Following the September 10, 2025, assassination of TPUSA co-founder Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University, the conservative organization reported receiving more than 120,000 inquiries from students seeking to establish local chapters. At Fort Lewis College, then-senior Jonah Flynn led the effort to establish a presence on campus. Although the Associated Students of Fort Lewis College (ASFLC) initially rejected Flynn’s proposal, the student government ultimately reversed course and voted to approve the group during an emergency session. The vote prompted immediate outrage from anti-TPUSA spectators waiting outside the meeting room. According to a Fort Lewis College campus police report, approximately 70 people attended the high-tension meeting. As attendees spilled out into the lobby, an argument broke out between attendees holding opposing views. The police report states that Peters approached a student who was "booing and yelling" while holding his phone about a foot away to record. The student — identified in police records as Megan Elizabeth Hope Mollett (who goes by Nova and uses they/them pronouns) — struck Peters' phone and hand with an empty Taco Bell cup. NEWLY LAUNCHED TPUSA CHAPTER CAUSES UPROAR AT MICHIGAN HIGH SCHOOL BEFORE FIRST MEETING Officers intervened immediately, separating the pair and detaining Mollett. While the incident was documented as harassment, police released Mollett with a warning after Peters declined to press criminal charges, though he requested that the university take internal disciplinary action. Reflecting on the fallout nearly a year later, Peters noted that the climate on campus remains hostile. During the same post-vote protest, David Kozak, a former anthropology professor at the college, was captured on video flipping off the camera and shouting at TPUSA supporters. "Go on, fascists," Kozak shouted. "Go on, Nazi lovers... C’mon, Nazis!" A spokesperson for Fort Lewis College confirmed to Fox News Digital that Kozak has since retired from the university. CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP The ongoing hostility comes as political violence remains a growing concern across the country following Kirk's assassination. Authorities cited political motivation in the shooting, pointing to evidence including ammunition allegedly engraved with political slogans, highlighting concerns over how inflammatory rhetoric is translating into real-world violence. Fort Lewis College did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment regarding Cook's and Peters' claims.

articles.title: EU condemns Serbia’s ministers for attending funeral of war criminal Mladic
articles.summary: EU leaders condemn Serbian officials’ presence at Ratko Mladic’s funeral as a failure to confront past war crimes.
articles.body:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa have condemned the presence of several senior Serbian officials at the funeral of war criminal Ratko Mladic.

The EU leaders said on Tuesday in identical statements published on X that images of the previous day’s commemoration in Serbia – a candidate for EU membership – were “shocking”.

“The elements of official support and the presence of some senior Serbian officials at the funeral are deeply regrettable,” they said on X. “They demonstrate a failure to confront a dark chapter in Europe’s recent history and contradict the values underpinning Serbia’s path towards the European Union.”

“Our thoughts are with all the victims of the crimes committed in the countries of former Yugoslavia,” they added.

Serbia’s Justice Minister Nenad Vujic had initially announced “military and state honours” for Mladic, drawing international protest and leading President Aleksandar Vucic to downgrade the event.

In attendance were Serbia’s defence and justice ministers, the head of the Serbian Orthodox Church, and officials from the Bosnian Serb separatist entity, Republika Srpska, including President Sinisa Karan.

Russia’s ambassador to Serbia, Alexander Botsan-Kharchenko, was also there.

Vucic himself did not attend the event. However, he described it as an “emotional outpouring”, and his son was present.

Mladic died in The Hague last month, aged 84, while serving a life sentence for genocide , war crimes and crimes against humanity during the 1990s Bosnian War. He remains a hero to many Serbs.

His legacy is linked to the 1995 Srebrenica genocide, when forces under his command captured a Bosniak enclave and systematically killed more than 8,000 men and boys, an atrocity that has been ruled a genocide by a United Nations court.

Bosnia downgraded diplomatic relations and recalled most of its embassy staff from Belgrade in response to the funeral.

The rebuke sharpens a standoff between Brussels and Belgrade, weeks before the bloc publishes its annual assessment of EU membership applicant countries.

Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos, charged with relations with candidate countries, had already cancelled a trip to Belgrade last week, saying the glorification of Mladic’s death would be incompatible with the blocs values and that the funeral would be “a test”.

Serbia’s membership prospects were already strained for other reasons. In April, Kos warned Belgrade it could lose access to about 1.5 billion euros ($1.8bn) in EU funds over irregularities in municipal elections.

Brussels has not yet announced how the incident will impact Serbia’s accession bid. Asked about possible consequences, von der Leyen’s spokesperson said the bloc was still “looking into it”.

Von der Leyen’s condemnation also drew questions from critics who have accused her of turning a blind eye to Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

Although Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is wanted in The Hague for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity against Palestinians, the EU has refused to cut off trade and diplomatic relations with the country.

In a post on X, Bruno Macaes, former Portuguese secretary of state for European affairs, called the condemnations “embarrassing” given that “the list of crimes being condemned corresponds exactly to the list of crimes that were excused or supported by these same governments over the last three years” in Gaza.

articles.title: Netanyahu faces backlash over report he was warned of Hamas attack days before October 7
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced a fierce political backlash Tuesday over a report that the president of the UAE had warned him of a major Hamas operation days before the October 7, 2023 attack.
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faced a fierce political backlash Tuesday over a report that the president of the UAE had warned him of a major Hamas operation days before the October 7, 2023 attack. The Prime Minister’s Office dismissed the report as an “absolute lie.” But with Israel’s October elections less than two months away, Netanyahu’s rivals seized on it as the latest evidence of what they say is a growing list of warnings he had ignored. The four opposition party leaders – Gadi Eisenkot, Naftali Bennett, Avigdor Lieberman and Yair Golan – issued a rare joint statement calling for “an immediate and thorough investigation” into Netanyahu’s “failures and malfunctioning.” “The Israeli public is entitled to know: What did Netanyahu know, when did he know, why he didn’t update the security establishment, and why he didn’t act to protect Israeli civilians?” the statement said. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett said the report is “true,” writing on X that Netanyahu’s alleged disregard for the warnings amounts to “criminal negligence.” Bennett’s political ally, former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, said he too had publicly warned of an attack before it happened, as had top Israeli security officials as well as Egyptian officials. “If Netanyahu had fulfilled his role, the massacre would have been prevented,” Lapid said in a statement. The report, published in the Haaretz newspaper, was based on findings from an upcoming book by Israeli journalists Shlomi Eldar and Ruti Yuval. It said UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed called Netanyahu about ten days before October 7, and during a 45-minute call, warned him that Hamas’ Gaza leader Yahya Sinwar was planning a major move against Israel that could cause bloodshed and destabilize the region. The report cited a message Sinwar conveyed to the UAE and Israel through a Palestinian mediator in mid-September 2023, warning of an upcoming “earthquake.” Haaretz reported that Netanyahu reacted “relatively calmly” to the information, and assured Bin Zayed that Israel was prepared for any scenario. CNN has reached out to the UAE Foreign Ministry for comment. The Prime Minister’s Office strongly denied the report, stating Netanyahu “did not speak with the president of the United Arab Emirates during the period in question and did not receive any warning from him.” Accountability as an electoral issue The report comes as Netanyahu’s rivals work to make accountability for October 7 – the deadliest attack in Israel’s history, during which over 1,200 people were murdered and more than 250 abducted to Gaza – a central campaign issue. Netanyahu has now outlasted nearly every member of Israel’s top security leadership from that day. Since the attack, the defense minister, the military chief of staff, and the directors of military intelligence, the Mossad and the Shin Bet, have all either resigned, been ousted, or reached the end of their terms. Gadi Eisenkot, currently polling as Netanyahu’s leading challenger, said the Haaretz report shows Netanyahu “led Israel blindly” toward the October 7 failures and renewed his pledge to establish a state commission of inquiry if elected. Nearly three years after the attack, Netanyahu has resisted demands from bereaved families and October 7 survivors to establish an independent commission to investigate the security and intelligence failures that enabled Hamas to conduct the operation. He and his associates have instead promoted a narrative blaming security chiefs for not waking him up the night before the attack despite intelligence indications that a Hamas offensive was imminent. Last month, his wife, Sara Netanyahu, suggested that Yair Golan – a retired major general and the leader of the left-wing Democrats party who independently rushed to the Gaza border on October 7 to rescue survivors – had advance knowledge of the attack. In an interview with the pro-government Channel 14, she questioned how Golan was “already dressed and ready” at dawn that day to head south, “while others knew nothing, including the prime minister.” Golan demanded an apology for what he called a “vile conspiracy theory” and said he would pursue a defamation suit, calling the allegation part of Netanyahu’s attempt to “rewrite” the events of October 7 and deflect responsibility. Following the Haaretz report, Golan wrote on X that the prime minister’s“they-didn’t-wake-me-up narrative is over. He knew, he was warned.” He called it “not an error in judgment, but a conscious and criminal abandonment.” Hours later, the Democrats party sharpened its electoral campaign against Netanyahu, erecting a giant billboard over Tel Aviv’s main highway bearing the headline: “The 1,200 murdered file – Causing death by negligence.”

articles.title: The shift in British policy on Israel is palpable
articles.summary: But progress could be threatened if there is a new more diplomatic government in Israel.
articles.body:
Fifty-nine years after Israel established its first illegal settlement in the occupied Palestinian territory, the United Kingdom has imposed a ban on trade with Israeli settlements. It is not before time, as the settler population numbers more than 750,000 residing in more than 140 formal settlements and more than 390 outposts and farms.

The ban comes as British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has promised a “comprehensive reset” in relations with Israel. This term is loaded – one he repeated multiple times in a meeting with me this week. A reset implies a realignment of the whole relationship, a strong term to choose to define the trajectory.

Is this a divorce, or a temporary separation? Is it just rhetoric or something more substantive? The foreign secretary told me he is determined to lead on this policy and do what he can to deter not just Israel’s settlement frenzy but its unparalleled aggression on the Palestinian people.

Is this seismic? Historically, it has been a close relationship with frequent road bumps but no crashes; a few marital spats but no more. In 1917, Britain authored the Balfour Declaration and presided over a disastrous mandate period in Palestine, leaving with war and ethnic cleansing in its wake.

In recent decades, the UK and Israel have enjoyed cosy relations, intense trade, defence and security cooperation, only interrupted by British statements of concern – occasionally deep concern – over Israel’s treatment of the Palestinian population.

March 2023 marked the high point of the British-Israeli relationship. The two governments signed the 2030 Roadmap for Bilateral Relations, envisioning close collaboration in all sectors, especially tech and security.

Then Prime Minister Rishi Sunak cemented this with fulsome support for Israel following the October 7 Hamas atrocities. Sunak stated: “I am unequivocal. We stand with Israel, not just today, not just tomorrow, but always.”

The UK-Israel relationship started deteriorating when Labour took over in 2024, not least due to the imposition of a partial arms ban. But Labour Prime Minister Keir Starmer was reluctant to hold Israel to account. Within the UK, he was largely viewed as a warm friend of Israel and was widely accused within his own party of having done little to nothing to stem the genocide, implementing only partial measures at the last moment. At no point did Starmer ever accuse Israel of violating international law in Gaza.

Yet in Israeli leadership circles, Starmer and his government were viewed as inherently anti-Israel, even as friends of Hamas who echoed the Palestinian group’s talking points. This view became more widespread after the UK’s recognition of the State of Palestine in 2025 and the sanctioning of two Israeli ministers, Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben-Gvir.

Since Andy Burnham took over in late July, the British tone has shifted dramatically. The evasive, hesitant rhetoric of Starmer has vanished, replaced by more strident statements placing the clear blame on Israel for its actions.

Burnham signalled a change even before he took his post. “Labour’s initial response to the treatment of Gaza caused huge hurt. We got it wrong and I am sorry for that,” he wrote on social media in early July. Downing Street has confirmed Burnham has yet to speak to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Foreign Secretary Miliband has been even more forthright. In his statement in response to the Israeli decision to move forward with tenders for E1, he pledged “a comprehensive set of measures to respond to Israeli government policies.” Comprehensive is another powerful term to let loose. Actions against arms sales are not ruled out.

All of this has shocked the Israeli political establishment. The assumption has been for years that European powers like Britain talk loud but would never wield a stick.

Official Israeli responses have framed the British government as anti-Semitic, whose policies are designed to appease the British Muslim vote. Netanyahu led the way by referring to the UK as the “Islamic Republic of Britain.”

The Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar fumed, “If Britain acts against the state of Israel, the state of Israel will act against Britain. We have tools.” Smotrich demanded the expulsion of the British ambassador to Israel, a measure the UK might reciprocate.

The US Ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, further fuelled the flames: “The Brits have lost it. The Jew hate of their government knows no boundaries and knows no facts.” Perhaps he did not know that Miliband is Jewish himself and a son of Jewish refugees.

Apart from upping its hostile rhetoric, what can Israel do? It can press the US to punish the UK. It can impose its own sanctions. It can kick the UK out of the International Gaza Support Centre, the body set up by the Board of Peace to monitor aid flows into Gaza. But it is highly likely that much of the retaliation will be taken out on Palestinians. There may be announcements of new settlements and other such measures to show Israel will proceed despite British sanctions.

At this point, is there a way back for the UK-Israeli relationship? With Netanyahu in power in Israel, and with a Labour government in charge in London, the answer is a clear no. If Netanyahu is dethroned and replaced by Gadi Eisenkot, a thaw might be possible.

The danger here is that any new Israeli government may be more diplomatic, less brash, but still pursue the same strategic policy towards the Palestinians. It is the policy, not the personnel, that matters.

The British government has to stay the course until Israel abandons its settlement industry. It should not be swayed by vague promises or less abrasive language. The measure of success can only be real change on the ground.
